actions.settingsText: `text` (string or list), `audience`: `player` (default with a player), `all` (default in global hooks), `world`, `nearby:<radius>`, `permission:<node>`

`text`, `color: red`, `overlay: progress` (or `notched_6/10/12/20`), `progress: 1.0`, `countdown-to`: `cycle-end`, a duration like `60s`, or a date-time `2026-12-01T00:00`; `seconds: 10` (how long an instant bar shows). Text variables: `<countdown>`, `<countdown_clock>`, `<seconds>`, plus every variable of the list it runs in (such as `<cycle>` in a hook). A timed bar shows while the action is active. In a global hook, everyone online sees it, including players who join while it runs, and it disappears when the countdown ends.
`text` (`<player> <x> <y> <z> <world>`), `audience: all`. Add `repeat` to report it regularly.
`command` or `commands` (list), `revert-commands`, `require-online: false`. `<player>`, `<uuid>` and every variable work.

actions.settingsText: what to match: `material`, `custom`, `name-contains`, `lore-contains`, `item-model`, `pdc` keys; `amount` (a number or `all`), `from`: `inventory`, `enderchest` or `both`, `return: true`. Never takes economy heads.
`slot`: `head`, `chest`, `legs`, `feet` or `offhand`; item definition; `lock: true` (can't be removed, survives death)
actions.undo: removes it and gives back what was in the slot

actions.settingsText: `owner`: `self`, a name or a UUID; `amount`; `cycle`: `current` or `next`; `to`: `inventory` or `vault`. Next-cycle heads go into the vault when the next cycle starts; heads that don't fit are delivered as items.

actions.undo: revokes it, if the player didn't already own it

actions.settingsText: `title`. It is equipped and locked for the duration.

timed: lifts the ban or mute

`state`: `on` or `off`, `lock: true` (the player can't toggle it while active), `restore: true`. Works with the included PvP or PvPManager; skipped with `pvp.provider: none`.
actions.undo: unlocks and restores the previous state

actions.settingsText: `ticks: 100`. Rain and water put it out, as in vanilla; a timed fire keeps relighting while active.
`food` (change in hunger), `exhaustion` (added every second while timed)

`deny`: any of `break`, `place`, `chat`, `commands`, `items`, `fly`, `elytra`, `ender-pearl`, `worlds`, `trade`, `shop`, `vault`, `interact`, `drop`, `pickup`, `attack`; plus `commands: [..]` (empty means all commands), `allowed-commands: [..]`, `items: [MATERIAL]` (empty means all items), `worlds: [..]`, `message`. Bypass with `headcount.bypass.deny.<category>`.

`starting-heads` and/or `vault-size`: `"+5"`, `"-3"` or `"=10"`. These add up across several actions and apply at the next cycle start. Extra starting heads that don't fit in the vault are delivered as items.
`percent: 50` sets this player's rollover for the next cycle end; `add: 10` adds to the current one
`charges: 0` (0 = unlimited). The player's head doesn't drop when they're killed.
`amount: 1`, `charges: 0`. Extra heads drop when the player is killed.
`flag`, `mode`: `set` or `clear`. Usable as a status (`source: flag`); timed: restores the previous state.
`amount`, added to this cycle's final score. Timed: removed again.
`choices: [{weight: 3, actions: [...]}, {weight: 1, list: other-list}]`. Picks one choice by weight.

options.help: Language file in plugins/Headcount/lang/, without .yml.
Date format for messages, as a Java DateTimeFormatter pattern. Dates show in the cycle time zone.
How many units a duration shows. With 2 a duration reads "3d 4h", with 3 it reads "3d 4h 12m". Unit names are in the lang file.
SQLite database file in plugins/Headcount/. Every change is saved as it happens.
Cycle
Length of a cycle in days. A change takes effect at the next cycle or the next /hca reset cycle. The running cycle keeps its end.
The day the first cycle starts, as YYYY-MM-DD, or "auto" to start right away, lined up to end-time today. Until a future date arrives, no cycle runs.
Time of day cycles roll over, as 24-hour HH:MM.

Time zone for start-date and end-time. Use a region like America/Denver or Europe/London (follows daylight saving), an abbreviation like MST or CET (a fixed offset all year, so MST is always UTC-7), an offset like GMT-7 or UTC+5:30, or "system". If the server was offline at a rollover, the next start ends the stored cycle and starts the one that should be running now. The cycle number goes up by one at each end. /hca reset cycle keeps the number and /hca reset hard starts again at 1. /hca cycle info also shows each cycle's internal run ID.
Playtime in a cycle needed to count as active. 0 means joining once is enough. Only active players get a score, points and outcomes.
How often playtime is saved and the active threshold checked.
Head vault (/hc)
Slots in each vault. Up to 54 fits on one screen. Bigger vaults are split into pages of 45. Size and starting heads change at the start of the next cycle or at a /hca reset cycle.

How many of their own heads each player starts a cycle with, up to the vault size. Extra starting heads from next-cycle actions, like a shop purchase or the streak bonus, are given as items if they don't fit.
Largest size the next-cycle vault-size action can grow a vault to.

Statuses (statuses.yml) that stop a player moving heads in or out of their vault. Each one has its own message, gates.vault-move.<status> in the lang file, and its own bypass permission, headcount.bypass.vault-move.<status>. Put ! before a status to block while it is NOT active.

Whether the same statuses also stop the vault from opening. With false, blocked players can still open it and look. Messages are gates.vault-open.<status> and the bypass is headcount.bypass.vault-open.<status>.
Whether the drop key (Q) on a vault slot drops the head on the ground. Normally players take it out first.
Whether a head whose ID is already in a vault can go in another one: reject | allow A second head with the same ID can only be a copy, usually from creative cloning.
Save the player's inventory to disk shortly after a vault change, so a crash can't roll back just one side.

Vault window title. Variables: <owner> <unique> <total> <size> <used> <page> <pages> <score>. <score> is the owner's score if the cycle ended now, or ? while the owner is offline. It uses score-colors below, or write <score:green:red:gray> to pick the positive, negative and zero colors right there. Any MiniMessage color or tag works, like #ff8800 or gold. The title updates while the vault is open.
Slots past the vault size on the last row.
The bottom row of paged vaults (more than 54 slots).

Enchantment glint on current heads.
Item model (namespace:key) for resource packs. Leave empty for the normal head.
Keep economy data on heads placed as blocks, and give it back whenever the block drops as an item again.
What breaking a head block in creative does: destroy | drop destroy drops nothing, like vanilla. drop gives the head back anyway.
Drop an economy head block that was removed without dropping anything, like from an explosion or a plugin.

How to treat head blocks with economy data that Headcount never saw placed: strip | allow These come from world editor copies or copied block data. strip turns them into plain heads and logs them as duplicates. allow trusts them.
Message admins with headcount.admin.notify when a duplicated head ID is found.
Remove extra copies found in an inventory. The copy already in a vault is kept. With false they are only flagged.
Check a player's inventory for duplicates whenever they close any inventory.
Kills

Killing a player drops a new head of the victim where they died. The head is made fresh, not taken from their vault, and it drops even with keepInventory on. The killer is whoever vanilla credits, so projectiles and knocking someone into lava count. Suicide gives nothing.
Only one head per killer per victim per cycle.
Heads dropped per kill. extra-heads actions add to this.
Worlds where kills drop nothing.
Statuses on the killer that stop a drop, like creative-or-spectator.
How long only the killer can pick up the head. 0 lets anyone.
Points (Headcount's own currency, not Vault money)
Percent of unspent points kept when a cycle ends. The rest are gone. A positive score gives points at the end of a cycle, to spend during the next one.
Points per score point, rounded down. With 1.0 a score of 7 gives 7 points.
Let balances go below zero when points are taken.
Messages, menus, placeholders
Minimum time between two "you can't do that while ..." messages to the same player.
Minimum time between two clicks in any Headcount menu. It stops fast clicks from buying something twice.
Text that true/false placeholders show, such as the status placeholders and active.
Lines shown by /hc top.
How often the live leaderboard refreshes. It feeds /hc top, %headcount_top_...% and ranks in previews.

The item for each past cycle. Variables: <cycle> <unique> <total> <own> <score> <earned> <spent> <rolled_over> <points_after> <streak> <rank> <outcomes> <playtime> <kills> <deaths> <trades> <ended> <player>

options.help: Sidebar
Turns Headcount's sidebar on for the server. Set false to show Headcount's placeholders in another scoreboard plugin instead. Players toggle their own with /hc sidebar.
Whether the sidebar starts shown for a player's first join. Players who already joined keep their choice.
How often the lines are redrawn.
Sidebar lines, up to 15. Headcount and PlaceholderAPI placeholders both work.
Audit log (plugins/Headcount/audit/)
Size in MB at which a log file rotates, at least 0.0625 (64 KB). Files also rotate daily.
Delete files older than this many days. 0 keeps them forever. Checked on start, on reload and each new day.
Gzip finished files.
Also print every audit line to the console.
Log every head moving in or out of a vault.
Log each head made at cycle start on its own line, instead of one summary line.
Lines per page in /hca audit.
Turn single event types off. All are on by default.
Resets (/hca reset cycle, /hca reset hard)

Whether a reset deletes the heads made before it, when the command doesn't say delete-heads or keep-heads. Old heads are worthless either way: they can't go in a vault and never count. true:   they are deleted wherever Headcount finds them - inventories and ender chests at the reset and on join, containers when opened, items picked up or dropped, and queued deliveries. false:  they stay as defunct heads (heads.item.defunct-name and defunct-lore). Each reset stores its choice, so changing this later doesn't affect earlier resets.

Allow /hca reset hard, which deletes every player's Headcount data and starts again from cycle 1. Config files are kept. It needs the headcount.admin.reset.hard permission, which the console always has.
How many new random codes the admin types to confirm, at least 1.
Time to type each code.
Copy the database to plugins/Headcount/backups/hard-reset-<time>/ first.
Move the audit log files there too, so the audit log starts empty.

Hooks: action lists that run at set moments in the cycle and when players join. Each list uses the actions system. actions.yml has every type and the common options. Cycle hooks (cycle-start, cycle-end and each warning) have two parts. cycle-start also runs after /hca reset cycle. global:      runs once for the server, with cycle-wide variables per-player:  runs once for each player, with their own variables players:   all | active | inactive | online offline:   deliver (store it and run it when they next join) | skip expire-after-cycles: stored hooks older than this many cycles are dropped actions:   the list Global variables: <cycle> <cycle_start> <cycle_end> <time_left> <cycle_length> <active> <players> cycle-end adds: <average_score> <rewarded> <punished> <top_list> <top_N_name> <top_N_unique> <top_N_score> Per-player variables at cycle-end: <player> <unique> <total> <own> <score> <rank> <percentile> <streak> <streak_text> <points_earned> <points> <rolled_over> <tier> <outcomes> <playtime> <kills> <deaths> <trades> Player hooks (player:) run for one player. When several run on the same join, they go in this order: delivered per-player cycle hooks, first-join, first-join-cycle, became-active, join. Variables: <player> <cycle> <time_left> <points> <streak> <streak_text>
Delay before join hooks run, so their messages come after the join message.
How late a warning can still fire if its moment passed while the server was offline.
How many players <top_list> lists.

options.help: Warnings before the end of a cycle. Each one needs 'before', how long before the end it fires.

options.default: [message: "<yellow>Cycle <cycle> ends in <white>3 days</white>. Fill your vault with unique heads! <gray>/hc"]

options.help: PvP: the PvP toggle, the combat tag and new-player protection. These feed the in-pvp, combat-tagged and newbie-protected statuses (statuses.yml) used by the default vault and trade rules, and the pvp action.

Which plugin handles PvP: included | pvpmanager | none included:   the built-in PvP, set up under 'included' below. It owns the /pvp command. pvpmanager: PvPManager does all of it, and the 'included' settings are ignored. none:       no PvP handling. Players can always fight, as in vanilla, and the PvP statuses read false. combat-tagged falls back to "hit by or hit a player in the last 15s" (statuses.yml).
---- Built-in PvP (provider: included) ----

PvP for players who never used /pvp: on | off With off, players opt in with /pvp before they can fight or be hit. That also keeps the default vault and trade rules, which block players with PvP on, out of their way.
Players can switch their own PvP with /pvp. They also need headcount.pvp, which everyone has by default.
Time between two switches. Bypass: headcount.bypass.pvp.cooldown
Put everyone back to the default each time they join.
Worlds where PvP is always on, whatever players chose, by exact world name. force-off-worlds keeps it off.
How long new players are protected after their first join, in real time. 0 turns it off. Protected players can't attack or be attacked.
A protected player can end it early with /pvp on.
How long nobody can hurt a player after they respawn. Attacking someone ends it. 0 turns it off.

Turns on the combat tag. A hit between two players puts them in combat (the combat-tagged status) for 'duration', and each new hit starts it over. A player's arrows, tridents, thrown potions, TNT and tamed pets count as their hits.
Tag the player who hits.
Tag the player who is hit.
End the tag when the player dies.
While in combat:

options.default: true           # flying stops and can't start again (never affects creative or spectator)
true         # teleports by commands and plugins (/spawn, /home, /tpa...) fail
[spawn, home, homes, warp, warps, tpa, tpahere, tpaccept, tpyes, back, rtp, wild, ec, enderchest, hub, lobby]
options.help: Commands that can't be used in combat, written without the slash. Namespaced forms like essentials:home are blocked too. Bypass for these and for teleports: headcount.bypass.combat-commands
Punish players who leave the server in combat. Kicks and bans don't count. Bypass: headcount.bypass.combat-log
What happens to the player who left: kill | none kill makes them die as they leave, so their items and XP drop where they stood. none only runs 'actions' and 'broadcast' below.
Give the kill to the player who last hit them, along with the kill head drop (config.yml kills).

Extra actions to run on the player who left. Any action from actions.yml works. Actions that need the player online wait until they next join. For example: actions: - type: points amount: -5 - message: "<red>You logged out during a fight and lost 5 points."
Tell everyone else. The message is pvp.combat-log-broadcast in the lang file.

How each kind of PvP message reaches the player. The texts are in lang/en_US.yml under pvp. channel: chat | actionbar | title | none sound:   a sound key like "minecraft:block.note_block.bass", or "" for none. volume and pitch: 0-2. A player gets the same message at most once a second.
/pvp switched your PvP (pvp.toggled-on / toggled-off / newbie-ended).
You hit someone or were hit, and are now in combat (pvp.tag-start).
Your combat tag ended (pvp.tag-end).
Your hit was stopped because the other player has PvP off or is protected (pvp.blocked-hit.*).
Something you tried was refused, like a blocked command or teleport, or /pvp during combat or a cooldown.
The live countdown while in combat (pvp.countdown): actionbar | bossbar | none
Boss bar color when countdown is bossbar: pink | blue | red | green | yellow | purple | white
---- PvPManager (provider: pvpmanager) ----

Let every player use PvPManager's /pvp. PvPManager keeps its pvpmanager.command.pvp permission from players by default, and they start with PvP on. Headcount's default rules block moving heads and trading while PvP is on, so players need a way to turn it off. This sets the permission's default to true. Anyone your permissions plugin explicitly denies stays denied. Set false to hand out the permission yourself.
Placeholders: %...% in Headcount's text, the score formula and statuses.

Which placeholders work: included | placeholderapi | none included:       only Headcount's %headcount_...% placeholders (listed in docs/placeholders.md). placeholderapi: those plus every PlaceholderAPI placeholder, and %headcount_...% for other plugins. none:           no %...% placeholders at all, not even Headcount's. They show as written.
Register the %headcount_...% expansion, so other plugins like scoreboards, tab and chat can show Headcount's data.
How formatted values like %headcount_title% are passed to other plugins: legacy | minimessage | plain
Money, for the money action. Points are Headcount's own currency and need nothing.
Which economy the money action uses: vault | none vault uses whatever economy plugin is behind Vault, like EssentialsX or CMI.
Permissions: the permission, group, primary-group, track, prefix and suffix actions, and title prefixes (titles.yml permission-prefix).

Which plugin handles permissions: included | luckperms | vault | none included:  Headcount sets permission nodes itself, saves them and re-applies them on every join. It can't do groups, tracks, prefixes or suffixes, so those actions are skipped with a warning. luckperms: everything, with LuckPerms' own expiry on timed changes. vault:     through Vault's permission API. Groups, prefixes and suffixes need a Vault chat plugin. none:      every permission action is skipped.
Give timed changes LuckPerms' own expiry too, so they still end if Headcount is removed.
"server" context for the nodes Headcount adds. Leave empty for global.
Moderation: the ban, mute, kick, warn and jail actions.

Which plugin handles moderation: included | litebans | libertybans | advancedban | essentials | commands | none included:    vanilla bans (the server's ban list), kicks, warnings sent as a message, and the built-in mute and jail set up below. commands:    any moderation plugin, driven by the command templates under 'commands'. none:        every moderation action is skipped. If a plugin can't do one kind, like jail in LibertyBans and LiteBans, that kind goes to 'included'.

A different provider for single kinds, with the same choices. For example, bans by LibertyBans but jail by EssentialsX: kinds: jail: essentials The kinds are ban, mute, kick, warn and jail. Kinds left out use 'provider'.
Name shown as the punisher, where the plugin supports it.
Hide punishment broadcasts, if the plugin allows it.
The built-in jail, used by 'included' and for jail with any plugin that has none.
Jail location as world,x,y,z[,yaw,pitch], like "world,0,64,0". Jail actions don't work until it is set.
Jailed players who get further away than this many blocks are pulled back.
Where release sends them: previous | spawn
Commands jailed players can still use. Everything else is blocked.
The built-in mute, used by 'included'. It blocks chat and these commands.
Commands used for LiteBans, since its API can't create punishments. Variables: <player> <uuid> <reason> <duration>
Command templates for provider 'commands'. Leave a kind empty if your plugin can't do it, and 'included' handles it instead. Variables: <player> <uuid> <reason> <duration> <jail>
Discord, for the discord action.
Which plugin sends Discord messages: discordsrv | none
DiscordSRV game channel for actions that don't name one.
Custom items: item definitions written as "custom: itemsadder:ns:id", "custom: oraxen:id", "custom: nexo:id".
Custom item plugins to use, out of itemsadder, oraxen and nexo. Ones that aren't installed are skipped, and [] turns custom items off.
Bedrock players, through Geyser. They get /trade accept instead of the chat link, and every menu and the sidebar work for them. This also feeds the bedrock status.
How Bedrock players are recognized: floodgate | geyser | none floodgate also knows players who have no Java account.
Player states: afk, vanished, god, jailed and muted, for the player-state status source (the afk and vanished statuses in statuses.yml).

Which plugin reports player states: included | essentials | none included:   AFK after 'afk.after' without activity, and vanished from the "vanished" flag most vanish plugins set. God mode comes from the player's invulnerable flag. Jailed and muted come from the built-in jail and mute, or from the moderation plugin when it can tell. essentials: EssentialsX's own /afk, /vanish, /god, jail and mute. none:       all five read false.
How long a player goes without moving, looking around, chatting, using commands or clicking before they are AFK. 0 means never.
Count turning the camera as activity.
Who is told when someone goes AFK or comes back: self | everyone | none (lang: player-state.*)
How %headcount_status_<name>% reads.
The player has PvP on, from the /pvp toggle of the PvP provider in integrations.yml. The default vault and trade rules block players while it's on. With provider none it is always false.
The player is in combat, from the PvP provider's combat tag. With provider none, recent-pvp-damage is used.
The player is vanished. Most vanish plugins set the "vanished" metadata this reads. With the essentials player-state provider, EssentialsX's /vanish counts too.
The player is AFK, from the player-state provider in integrations.yml: the built-in idle timer or EssentialsX's /afk.
How long a request waits before it expires.
Status (statuses.yml) that makes a target count as offline, so vanished staff aren't revealed.
Countdown between both players confirming and the trade going through. Both sides are locked meanwhile. Any change to either side clears both confirmations.
Time both players wait before their next trade. Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade.cooldown
Also start the cooldown when a trade is cancelled.
Maximum distance between the players in blocks. -1 means no limit. Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade.range
Both players must be in the same world.
Which kinds of trade are allowed. "Heads" are economy heads of the current cycle. Anything else, expired heads included, is an "item".
Trades where one side offers nothing.
Most item stacks one side can offer, not counting heads.
Most economy heads one side can offer.
Players can only offer their own heads.
Materials that can never be traded.

Statuses that stop a request from being sent, checked on both players. The sender sees gates.trade-send.<status> or gates.trade-send-target.<status>, depending on who has it. Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade-send.<status>
Statuses that stop a request from being accepted, checked on both players. Messages are gates.trade-accept.<status> and gates.trade-accept-target.<status>.
Statuses that cancel an open trade, checked on both players every cancel.check-interval. Bypass: headcount.bypass.trade-cancel.<status>

When an open trade is cancelled, everything goes back to its owner. It always cancels if either player closes the screen, leaves, dies, changes world, goes out of range or gets a cancel status, and when the cycle ends or the server stops or reloads.
Also cancel when either player teleports.
Teleports shorter than this many blocks, within the same world, don't cancel.
Also cancel when either player's game mode changes.
How often open trades are checked for range, statuses and closed screens.
Save both players' inventories to disk when a trade completes, and about a second after any item moves in or out of an offer. A crash then can't duplicate or lose offered items.
Trade window title. Every text in this menu can use <other> <seconds> <my_heads> <my_items> <their_heads> <their_items> <max_heads> <max_items>
Slots for your offer, on the left. other-slots holds the other player's offer. Both lists must be the same length.

options.default: ["<gray>Your offer is on the left.", "<gray>Heads: <white><my_heads>/<max_heads></white> · Items: <white><my_items>/<max_items>", "<gray>Their offer: <white><their_heads></white> heads, <white><their_items></white> items"]
["<gray>Both players must confirm.", "<gray>Any change clears both."]
["<gray>Both sides are locked.", "<gray>Click confirm to stop."]

options.help: The score formula, worked out for each active player when a cycle ends. It takes normal math: + - * / % (remainder) ^ (power), parentheses, comparisons (< <= > >= == !=, which give 1 or 0), && || !, and "condition ? a : b". Functions: min(a, b, ...) max(...) avg(...) floor ceil round(x[, digits]) trunc abs sign pow(x, y) sqrt cbrt exp log(x[, base]) ln log10 log2 clamp(x, low, high) if(condition, a, b) sin cos tan Constants: pi e true false Variables: unique            unique heads in the vault, from different owners (your own head counts once) total             all heads in the vault, duplicates included own               copies of your own head in the vault duplicates        total - unique vault_size        your vault slots this cycle vault_free        empty vault slots starting_heads    heads every vault started with this cycle active            active players this cycle players           everyone who has ever joined online            players online now rank              your rank among active players by unique heads, 1 being the most (ties share a rank) percentile        your percentile among active players, from 0 at the bottom to 100 at the top unique_avg, unique_median, unique_max, unique_min, unique_sum unique heads over all active players kills             kill heads you got this cycle deaths            kill heads others got from you trades            completed trades heads_in          heads received through trades heads_out         heads given through trades purchases         shop purchases this cycle points_spent      points spent this cycle points            points you hold now points_next       points already waiting for next cycle playtime          minutes played this cycle playtime_hours    hours played this cycle streak            +N after N positive cycles in a row, -N after N negative ones streak_positive   the length of a positive streak, else 0 streak_negative   the length of a negative streak, else 0 last_score        last cycle's score, or 0 if there was none last_unique       last cycle's unique heads has_last          1 if there was a last score bonus             score bonus from actions (see add-bonus-after-formula) titles            titles you own cycle             the cycle ID cycle_length      cycle length in days days_elapsed      days since the cycle started days_left         days until it ends is_active         1 if you are active %any_placeholder% any numeric PlaceholderAPI placeholder, like %statistic_player_kills%. For offline players it gives whatever the placeholder supports. Anything that isn't a number counts as 0. Other formulas to try (copy one into 'formula'): Exponential, rewarding big collections:   floor(pow(unique, 1.5) / 2) - ceil(active / 4) Percent-based, compared to everyone:      round((percentile - 50) / 10) Rank-based, top 3 rewarded:               rank <= 3 ? 10 - rank * 2 : (percentile < 25 ? -3 : 0) Share of all active players collected:    round(unique / max(active, 1) * 10) - 5 Streak bonus on top of the default:       unique - ceil(active / 4) + min(streak_positive, 3) Punish hoarding your own head:            unique - ceil(active / 4) - floor(own / 10) Kills matter:                             unique + kills - deaths - ceil(active / 4) The default gives one point per unique head, minus a quarter of the active players rounded up. With 12 active players, 3 unique heads scores 0 and 10 unique heads scores 7.
How the formula's result is rounded to a whole number: floor | round | ceil
Add the total from 'score-bonus' actions after the formula and rounding. Set false if your formula uses 'bonus'.
How tied scores are ranked: competition | dense Scores of 10, 10 and 8 rank 1, 1, 3 with competition and 1, 1, 2 with dense.
What a cycle without activity does to a streak: pause | break pause keeps the streak and break resets it to 0. A streak counts cycles in a row with a positive score, or in a row with a negative one.
What a score of exactly 0 does to a streak: break | pause

Which matching rules a player gets. With all, they get every rule their score matches. With most-extreme, they get only the most extreme match in each group, so a score of -12 gets the severe penalty and not all three.
Bans a player for a day after three negative cycles in a row. Off by default.

options.default: "Three negative Headcount cycles in a row"

options.help: Bans a player permanently for a score of -25 or lower. Off by default.

options.default: [message: "<aqua><streak> good cycles in a row. You start next cycle with 3 extra heads.", type: next-cycle]

options.help: Price at which a purchase asks for confirmation first. An entry can override this with confirm: true or false.
Last-cycle score for players who don't have one, because they are new or were inactive.
When global stock refills: cycle or never.
Menu title. Variables: <tier> <tier_id> <tier_number> <tiers> <page> <pages> <points> <last_score> <threshold> <needed>

options.default: ["<gray>Tier: <tier> <dark_gray>(<tier_number>/<tiers>)", "<gray>Your last cycle score: <white><last_score>", "<gray>You earn points with a positive score."]
["<gray>Needs a last cycle score of <white><threshold></white> or more.", "<gray>Yours was <white><last_score></white> (<white><needed></white> more needed)."]

options.help: Confirmation menu for expensive purchases. The entry being bought is shown in the 'display' slot.

Default look of entries in each state. An entry's own 'display' and 'display-states' override these. The states are affordable, too-expensive, sold-out and locked, plus three optional ones. If left out, limit-reached looks like sold-out, and cooldown and unavailable look like too-expensive. Variables: <name> <price> <points> <missing> <stock> <purchases_left> <limit> <bought> <cooldown> <tier> <threshold>

options.default: ["<gray>Price: <gold><price> points", "<gray>Stock: <white><stock></white> · Left for you this cycle: <white><purchases_left>", "", "<green>Click to buy"]
["<gray>Price: <gold><price> points", "<red>You reached the limit of <limit> for this cycle."]
["<gray>Price: <gold><price> points", "<red>You don't meet the requirements for this."]

options.help: The shop's tiers, in order. A tier with 'threshold: none' is always unlocked. Tier settings: name, threshold (a last-cycle score, or none), pages (the minimum; entries can add more), enabled and entries. Entry settings: name                 the entry's name in messages (default: its display name without formatting) enabled              false hides it page, slot           where it goes (page starts at 1) price                in points display              item definition (material, name, lore, item-model, glint, enchants, custom ...) display-states       per-state overrides (affordable, too-expensive, sold-out, locked, limit-reached, cooldown, unavailable) actions              what a purchase does limit-per-cycle      purchases per player per cycle (0 = no limit) stock                global stock (-1 = unlimited) cooldown             time between purchases per player conditions           extra requirements (see actions.yml) requires             titles: [..], purchases: [entry or tier.entry, ever], purchases-this-cycle: [..], permissions: [..] confirm              force the confirmation menu on (true) or off (false)

options.default: ["<gray>Heads that don't fit in your vault", "<gray>are given to you as items."]
"<gold>A shield protects you from your next punishment."
["<gray>Your head does not drop when you are killed."]
"<gold>5 of your heads in next cycle's vault"

options.help: What %headcount_title% shows when nothing is equipped.
How %headcount_title% shows the equipped title. <title> is the title's display text.
Equip a player's first title automatically.
Copies the shown title into your permissions plugin as a prefix or suffix, with colors converted to legacy &-codes.

Turns the prefix or suffix on. A change applied with /hca reload updates online players right away, and others when they next join while it is on. A prefix left over from before it was turned off has to be removed with your permissions plugin.
Whether the title is set as a prefix or a suffix.
Priority of the prefix or suffix. Headcount clears anything else at this priority, so pick one nothing else uses.

The titles players can own. Each key (champion, collector...) is the title's ID for /hca title, the grant-title action and shop requirements. display       what players see, in MiniMessage description   lore lines in the menu icon          the menu item, as an item definition (see config.yml) enabled       false hides the title
Menu title. Variables: <page>
Show titles the player doesn't own, as locked.
How each title looks in the menu, combined with the title's own 'icon'. States: owned, equipped, forced, locked. Variables: <title> <id> <description>

{ slot: 53, material: ARROW, name: "<yellow>Next page", lore: ["<gray>Page <page> of <pages>"] }

recipes.title: A weekly cycle that ends Sunday evening
yaml:
# config.yml
cycle:
  length-days: 7
  start-date: 2026-11-15      # a Sunday
  end-time: "20:00"
  time-zone: America/Denver

recipes.title: Hardcore: harsh punishments and bans for repeat offenders
yaml:
# outcomes.yml
mode: all                      # every matching rule applies
rules:
  ban-repeat-offenders:
    enabled: true
# actions.yml: make punish-mild stronger
  punish-mild:
    - message: "<red>Score <score>. You are slowed for a full day."
    - type: potion
      effect: slowness
      amplifier: 1
      duration: 1d

recipes.title: Points carry over, and big collections are rewarded more
yaml:
# config.yml
points:
  rollover-percent: 50
# scoring.yml
formula: "floor(pow(unique, 1.5) / 2) - ceil(active / 4)"

recipes.title: Using another combat plugin through PlaceholderAPI
yaml:
# statuses.yml
  combat-tagged:
    source: placeholder
    placeholder: "%combatlogx_in_combat%"
    operator: equals
    value: "Yes"
    fallback: recent-pvp-damage

recipes.title: Only count players who actually play
Another scoreboard plugin shows Headcount instead
recipes.text: Then use `%headcount_unique%`, `%headcount_score%`, `%headcount_points%`, `%headcount_time_left%` and `%headcount_streak_text%` in that plugin.

recipes.title: Titles as LuckPerms prefixes
yaml:
# titles.yml
settings:
  permission-prefix:
    enabled: true
    type: prefix
    priority: 100

recipes.title: A shop entry that rents a rank for three days
yaml:
# shop.yml, under a tier's entries
      vip-rental:
        slot: 22
        price: 30
        limit-per-cycle: 1
        display: { material: GOLD_INGOT, name: "<gold>VIP for 3 days" }
        actions:
          - type: group
            group: vip
            duration: 3d
            start-message: "<gold>You are VIP for <duration>."
            end-message: "<gray>Your VIP rental ended."

recipes.title: A punishment that locks PvP on
yaml:
# actions.yml
  punish-pvp:
    - type: pvp
      state: on
      lock: true
      duration: 1d
      start-message: "<red>Your PvP is forced on for a day."

recipes.title: PvP always on in the Nether, and logging out of a fight costs points
yaml:
# integrations.yml
pvp:
  included:
    toggle:
      force-on-worlds: [world_nether]
    combat-log:
      actions:
        - type: points
          amount: -5
        - message: "<red>You logged out during a fight and lost 5 points."

recipes.title: Everyone fights by default, with a longer combat tag
recipes.text: With PvP on by default, the default vault and trade blocks for `in-pvp` apply to everyone until they turn PvP off. If you don't want that, remove `in-pvp` from `vault.block-movement.statuses` and from the trade statuses.
yaml:
# integrations.yml
pvp:
  included:
    toggle:
      default: "on"
    combat-tag:
      duration: 30s
      block-elytra: true
      block-ender-pearls: true
    messages:
      countdown: bossbar

recipes.title: Bans by LibertyBans, jail by EssentialsX
yaml:
# integrations.yml
moderation:
  provider: libertybans
  kinds:
    jail: essentials

recipes.title: Time zone as an abbreviation or offset
recipes.text: Abbreviations and offsets are fixed: `MST` is UTC-7 all year. A region such as `America/Denver` follows daylight saving.
yaml:
# config.yml
cycle:
  time-zone: MST        # or GMT-7, UTC+5:30, America/Denver, system
